penzack.thesis: Frontend Engineering for Penzack at AZX, an investment and trading platform with 1M+ users.
penzack.context: Penzack is the international investment and trading product developed at AZX, my employer. The platform serves more than one million users.
penzack.challenge: Support onboarding, identity verification and financial transactions across regional markets and languages, alongside real-time trading experiences.
penzack.responsibility: Build and maintain frontend features with React, Next.js and TypeScript. Collaborate with international teams in English on authentication, onboarding, KYC, trading interfaces and transaction flows. Contributed to Core Web Vitals improvements without a quantified performance claim.
penzack.solution: Implemented automatic sign-in, email verification and KYC status handling, plus deposit and withdrawal interfaces including Pix and OXXO. Use Zustand and TanStack Query for application state and API data. Contributed to Next.js App Router and Server Actions modernization, browser compatibility fixes, multilingual responsive interfaces and Sentry production error monitoring.
penzack.impact: Delivered financial and onboarding features within a platform serving 1M+ users, with support for regional payment journeys and multilingual experiences.
penzack.decisions: Frontend modernization alongside financial features requires care around API data, application state and existing user journeys. Core Web Vitals improvements are described qualitatively; no before/after benchmark is available.
penzack.lesson: Scale belongs to the platform. My contribution is the frontend workflows and modernization described above, delivered with the wider team.

james-moto-shop.thesis: End-to-end development of a commercial platform connecting a public portal and ERP, handling 1,000+ leads per month.
james-moto-shop.context: A consortium sales business needing a public-facing website connected to its administrative ERP.
james-moto-shop.challenge: Connect lead acquisition and the lead-to-contract journey with administrative operations, while keeping the product maintainable and visible in search.
james-moto-shop.responsibility: Led two developers and one designer delivering a React/Node.js sales platform with ERP integration and 1,000+ leads per month. Owned architecture, coordinated delivery and refined lead-to-contract workflows.
james-moto-shop.solution: Built the portal and ERP integration with Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Node.js and Prisma. Used AWS EC2, S3 and RDS for cloud deployment and refined checkout and conversion flows through UX improvements.
james-moto-shop.impact: Delivered a commercial platform processing more than 1,000 leads per month, connecting the public website to administrative operations.

bullets.b2: Technical leadership across portal and ERP

james-moto-shop.decisions: The portal, backend and ERP serve different parts of the same sales journey. The approach connects them with a React/Node.js stack; no unverified conversion uplift is attributed to that choice.
james-moto-shop.lesson: Ownership spans architecture, team coordination and the lead-to-contract workflow. The 1,000+ monthly leads describe platform usage, while the leadership scope is two developers and one designer.

elint.thesis: React to Next.js modernization and analytics dashboards for enterprise clients.
elint.context: Enterprise applications serving clients including Lacta and Universal Music, with reporting and data visualization needs.
elint.challenge: Modernize a large React application and make operational data easier to analyze and export.
elint.responsibility: Developed and maintained frontend features, migrated an application from Create React App to Next.js and implemented analytics interfaces.
elint.solution: Migrated the existing React application to Next.js. Built interactive charts with Recharts and added report export capabilities for operational analysis.
elint.impact: Delivered a Next.js migration and interactive analytics dashboards with report exports for enterprise products.

bullets.b1: Create React App to Next.js migration

elint.decisions: Migrating from Create React App to Next.js changes the application foundation. The documented scope is the migration and analytics interfaces; specific rollout or rollback strategies are not claimed.
elint.lesson: Modernization includes making operational data useful: interactive dashboards and report exports accompany the framework migration.

desencoder.thesis: Full-stack delivery of custom web applications and financial transaction workflows.
desencoder.context: Custom React applications and integrations for business and fintech workflows.
desencoder.challenge: Translate operational requirements into web applications and connect financial user journeys with backend services.
desencoder.responsibility: Designed and delivered custom web applications, developed a fintech solution and collaborated with cross-functional teams under demanding timelines.
desencoder.solution: Connected React application workflows with backend services and business integrations. Specific security mechanisms are not documented in this case.
desencoder.impact: Delivered business applications connecting frontend experiences with backend services for production users.
desencoder.decisions: Frontend workflows depend on the business capabilities exposed by backend services. This case stays at that integration boundary rather than describing undocumented infrastructure or security mechanisms.
desencoder.lesson: End-to-end delivery means connecting interface behavior with business operations and collaborating across disciplines. Product scale is not an individual performance metric.

facil-crm.thesis: Built AI-powered CRM workflows with collaborating agents and Go APIs connecting intelligent services to legacy business systems.
facil-crm.context: Customer operations depend on business information held in existing enterprise systems.
facil-crm.challenge: Connect AI-assisted operations to legacy business capabilities through an integration layer.
facil-crm.responsibility: Built collaborating-agent workflows and Go APIs for accessing legacy client systems.
facil-crm.solution: Go APIs provide a boundary between the agent workflows and existing business systems. The diagram describes this integration at a conceptual level; agent frameworks and deployment details are not disclosed.
facil-crm.impact: Connected AI capabilities to legacy business workflows. Production scope and quantitative outcomes are not documented here.
facil-crm.decisions: The Go API boundary connects agent workflows to existing systems without presenting those systems as native AI services. Authentication, evaluation and deployment details are outside the documented scope.
facil-crm.lesson: An agent workflow needs access to business capabilities through explicit integrations. This case documents those connections, without promising autonomous resolution or a measured service level.

tactia-build.thesis: Solution design for consolidating fragmented business workflows and connecting enterprise systems.
tactia-build.context: Business teams often depend on separate tools and disconnected operational information.
tactia-build.challenge: Map operational needs and identify where custom software and integrations can simplify the workflow.
tactia-build.responsibility: Worked on business system and integration design. This overview is limited to solution design; individual client deliveries are not documented.
tactia-build.solution: A conceptual view of connecting existing tools through integrations and a coherent operational interface. The diagram illustrates the approach, not a deployed client architecture.
tactia-build.impact: A modernization approach focused on coherent operations. No production rollout, client count or measured efficiency gain is claimed.
tactia-build.decisions: Integration can connect existing tools, while custom software can consolidate a workflow. The appropriate boundary depends on discovery; no particular client architecture is claimed here.
tactia-build.lesson: Solution design is distinct from delivery evidence. Client-specific implementation, screenshots and measured outcomes remain outside this overview.

tactia-ai.thesis: Implemented a Python workflow orchestration proof of concept using Hatchet, PostgreSQL and Docker workers, with automated tests for asynchronous tasks.
tactia-ai.context: AI-related tasks need coordination beyond a synchronous request. This project explores that infrastructure as a proof of concept.
tactia-ai.challenge: Separate asynchronous execution from workflow coordination and verify the behavior with automated tests.
tactia-ai.responsibility: Implemented the Python/Hatchet orchestration POC, Docker workers, PostgreSQL integration and unit/integration tests.
tactia-ai.solution: Hatchet coordinates asynchronous work executed by Python workers in Docker, with PostgreSQL persistence. Unit and integration tests exercise task execution. Production hardening remains future work.
tactia-ai.impact: An initial, tested orchestration foundation. This is a proof of concept, with no claim of production scale or customer adoption.
tactia-ai.decisions: Separating workers from workflow coordination makes asynchronous execution explicit, while adding infrastructure to operate. Docker, PostgreSQL and Hatchet are part of this POC; production reliability has not been established here.
tactia-ai.lesson: Unit and integration tests support confidence in task execution within the POC. Load testing and production hardening are future validation steps, not delivered outcomes.
